designs.title: Fanad Head Lighthouse
designs.why: Well-built poster: strong arched slab heading, neat data columns (facts check out), rich cliff-and-surf engraving that holds detail at full size. But on the black main tee the art is printed unreversed, so the white tower and keepers' houses turn into dark silhouettes and the scene reads like a photo negative. The lower half is a dense mass of texture with no tonal rest, and the hard rectangular frame makes it read as a poster stuck on a shirt.
designs.fix: Make a reversed (knock-out) version of the art for the black tee so the tower and buildings print as ink-white and the sea and shadows drop out to the shirt colour.

designs.title: Portland Head Light
designs.why: The best-known subject, and an accurate one: the keeper's house and the tower on the ledge make a good composition, and the dates and coordinates are correct. But the condensed PORTLANDHEAD heading is set with almost no word space and crowds the frame. The tower is pushed right and is thinner than the house, so the house pulls focus. On black the tower again inverts to a dark shape.
designs.fix: Open the word space and tighten the heading's tracking, then make the tower bigger and reverse the art for the black tee so the white tower is the brightest thing in the frame.

designs.title: Cape Agulhas Lighthouse
designs.why: The banded tower is a strong graphic icon and the heading is the cleanest of the four. But it has only two data lines, which leaves big dead areas on both sides of the tower, and the bottom 40% is undifferentiated rock-and-scrub texture that turns to noise on the tee. The flanking pylons and the residence read flat and stiff next to the tower. On black the bands flip, which is less of a problem here, but the scene still reads as a negative.
designs.fix: Cut the foreground scrub band down and let the tower and building sit bigger and lower in the frame, filling the side voids with a third data pair (e.g. southernmost tip of Africa / where two oceans meet).

designs.title: Phare de Saint-Mathieu
designs.why: The most distinctive of the set: the ruined abbey next to the tower gives it a story and a silhouette none of the others have. The two-tier PHARE DE / SAINT-MATHIEU heading with the Plougonvelin · Finistere · Bretagne line has real hierarchy, and the facts are right. The engraving is dense but legible. Its weak spots: the abbey's heavy blacks fill in at small size, and on the black tee the white tower goes dark.
designs.fix: Supply a reversed separation for the black tee and open up the abbey's solid blacks with hatching so it does not plug when printed.
